David Epstein's argument in one sentence.
Elite skill is not fast reflexes, and it is not 10,000 hours.
It's learned pattern recognition,

The answer is chunking. The chain of research goes like this. In

Then in 1973, William Chase and Herbert

random arrangements of pieces that could

completely. Their memories became
ordinary. That is the crucial experiment, because it proves the
advantage is learned, not an innately
miraculous memory. Chase and Simon's explanation is chunking
theory. Experts don't remember 20 individual
pieces. They unconsciously group information into a small number
of meaningful chunks based on patterns
they've seen before. A grandmaster has something like 300,000

of language for the chess master to say that he sees the right

board. He was, in Epstein's phrase, stripped of his crystal
ball. And the summary line from the experts

The origin is a 1993 study at the Music Academy of West Berlin
by K. Anders Ericsson and colleagues.
They compared the best violin students, good students, and
future music teachers. All three
groups spend about the same total time on music, around 50 hours

It's cross-sectional and retrospective. The subjects had already

academy, so most of humanity had been screened out before the

biased against ever discovering innate talent. And Ericsson
himself later conceded the data came from
only 10 individuals whose own estimates didn't perfectly agree
